sentences.text: Spondylosoma is a genus of avemetatarsalian archosaurs, a group that includes dinosaurs and pterosaurs, belonging to the clade Aphanosauria.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of two teeth, cervical and dorsal vertebrae, sacral vertebrae, scapulae, and partial limb bones.
Friedrich von Huene established the genus based on a fragmentary postcranial skeleton housed at the University of Tübingen.
Von Huene originally classified Spondylosoma as a prosauropod.
Redescriptions of related taxa like Teleocrater led to the referral of Spondylosoma to the new clade Aphanosauria.
Spondylosoma lived between 241.464 and 237 million years ago during the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic.
Fossils of Spondylosoma were found in the lower part of the Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
Scientists have debated whether Spondylosoma is a basal dinosaur, a thecodont, or another type of basal archosaur.
In 2000, Peter Galton argued that Spondylosoma lacks dinosaurian traits and is likely a rauisuchian related to rauisuchids.
In 2004, Max Langer disputed Galton's view, suggesting Spondylosoma might be a basal dinosaur related to herrerasaurs while leaving rauisuchian affinities open.
Sterling Nesbitt placed Spondylosoma in Archosauria incertae sedis in his 2009 thesis due to insufficient characters to place it in Pseudosuchia or Ornithodira.
